requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.references.outline_comments`. I did not request any implementation source. Each obligation maps to a marked test with assertions that enforce it. All tests are in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` unless another file is named.

- **Run formation and the next-node rule.**
  - `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` checks that two consecutive comment lines both belong to the following `fn[b]`.
  - `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers runs separated from the next node by a blank line, runs inside a node, a floating run that ends up with the container `mod[m]`, and a final top-level run that ends up with the root.
- **Container fallback.**
  - `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` cover a run with no following node, inside a mod and at top level.
- **Trailing comments.**
  - `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` checks that a comment following code on the same line belongs to the innermost node containing that line. It also checks that the next line's comment forms a separate run owned by the next node.
  - `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers the "including another comment" case. The first comment goes to `fn[b]` and the second to the root.
- **Rust inner doc comments.**
  - `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` checks that `//!` and `/*!` at file level belong to the root.
  - `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` checks that a `//!` inside `mod m` belongs to `mod[m]`, even though a node follows it. The same test shows that `// above inner` directly after it belongs to `fn[inner]`, so inner doc comments are not merged into the run of ordinary comments.
- **Every supported language.**
  - `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown with a leading run, a trailing comment, and a container or tail case.
  - `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` and `tests/repository.rs#fn[workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows]` add YAML cases.
- **Markdown profile.** `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` asserts three things. Only the block is a comment. The inline `<!-- -->` lies in no comment span. The owner of that line is a `paragraph` node.
- **A reference counts for its run's node.** This obligation is checked by the marked tests below, which assert owners or contributed items:
  - `src/fenced.rs` `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run`: fence owners and run-bounded closing.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs` `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes`: the contributed `fn[gap]` item.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs` `search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners`: a comment match is attributed to its owner.
  - `src/evidence.rs` `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node`: digests that change with the owning node.
  - `src/structural.rs` `matches_belong_to_the_innermost_node_or_comment_owner`: comment matches attributed to their owner.

I found minor untested corners, and I do not count them as gaps. One is a Python comment indented after a class's last node. Another is a `/*! */` block inside a mod. A third is a comment that precedes code on the same line. The text does not name these as separate cases, and the generic rule is checked in several other languages.

:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
